units.stage1_answer: The opening treats persistence as the question. The revised map promises spike action before eye-angle coding, and both now occur in that order. No claim about the source of persistence is added here.
The held-eye requirement is muscle force, while rate is an expected count per time rather than periodic spikes. Moving these definitions before anatomy does not change their meanings.

Muscles rotate the eyeball; OMNs activate muscles through cranial nerves; torque is the turning effect of force. The moved passage keeps orientation dependence and opposing muscle tension, so the new first location does not imply a one-muscle one-angle rule.

The actor is repeated motor activity, which maintains force beyond individual electrical events. Tonic activity need not be periodic. Elasticity supplies the restoring tendency; damping and inertia do not supply static holding torque. These claims do not rely on the later mechanical equation to be true.

The bridge now asks which firing pattern represents an angle already connected to muscle action. Synapses, excitatory and inhibitory input, and recurrent feedback are taught before their model role. The local tuning curve keeps its positive-rate range and threshold caveat.

The rate vector identifies cells rather than physical positions. Spatial examples retain the distinction between a place field, finite-recording rate map, and repeated grid fields. The move does not change these statements or turn the eye coding example into a spatial neuron map.

The revised opening correctly points to the newly taught pathway. The bridge separates mechanical force balance from maintenance of the neural command; it does not claim that eye anatomy itself proves a continuous attractor.

The equation is an explicitly limited small-angle teaching approximation. Zero velocity and acceleration give active torque K times angle. Removing torque and neglecting inertia gives exponential relaxation with B/K. All symbols, conditions and nonlinear-mechanics limits remain in Chapter 2.

The neural integrator is defined as accumulating movement commands into maintained position. The monkey disruption evidence and the goldfish visual-feedback plasticity evidence remain distinct. The passage keeps the warning that the goldfish experiment did not identify the cellular learning rule.

Recurrent correction of some disturbances is distinguished from a lasting shift to another represented angle. State, fixed point, neutral direction and manifold dimension retain their definitions. The bridge identifies the next model as an isolated question rather than a fitted biological circuit.

The changed link points to the moved motor-action teaching. The main text still distinguishes recorded shared upstream drive from the proposed continuous-attractor source. OMNs and ocular plant retain their separate roles.

Entries 7 to 11 retain anatomy, mechanics, plasticity, Poisson background and integrator disruption sources. The new order matches anatomy then mechanics then plasticity then Poisson then the Chapter 2 integrator experiment after the earlier six source entries.
